title: Research efficient multi-agent delivery from ClearFront evidence
description: Operator-directed comparative study of how ClearFront was handled, focused on process rather than another product/code audit. Use the project task/event/artifact/hcom record as empirical evidence; compare it with current primary-source guidance and published evidence on AI-agent orchestration, software delivery performance, lean flow, incident response, high-reliability operations, and organizational coordination. Identify what MAP does well, where it gets in its own way, which practices transfer, which do not, and a prioritized experiment-backed improvement roadmap. Broad learning is encouraged, but recommendations must reduce or measurably justify coordination cost rather than add ceremony.
acceptance_criteria: Study uses concrete ClearFront lifecycle evidence and quantifies process characteristics where records allow.
Study compares at least four current agent-orchestration approaches using primary sources and distinguishes workflow patterns from marketing claims.
Study draws on at least four established real-world operating disciplines or business examples, with sourced mechanisms rather than analogy alone.
Recommendations identify adopt/avoid/pilot decisions, expected benefit, cost/risk, measurable success criteria, and implementation priority.
Artifact separates verified facts, source-backed inference, and proposals; includes citations/links and evidence limitations.
